text:
Mark Scheifele's goal midway through the second period tied the game 3-3, and it was more than an equalizer. As The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted, it moved him past Dale Hawerchuk for the most goals in Jets history. Winnipeg had the lead in the third and the night set up for a celebration. Vegas took it away.

The start was rough for Carter Hart again: Adam Lowry tipped in the first shot of the game 29 seconds in, the second straight start, per Granger, in which the first shot Hart faced went in. But the Golden Knights owned the first period, 2.44 expected goals (the quality of their chances) to 1.01, and Brett Howden and Mitch Marner turned it into a 2-1 lead. Viggo Björck tied it late in the period. Tomas Hertl batted in a power-play chance in the second, a 63% look and the best of the night, before Scheifele answered.

Kyle Connor gave Winnipeg a 4-3 lead early in the third with a wrist shot, and our win probability had the Jets at 78%. At 16:25 of the third, Ivan Barbashev scored off feeds from Hertl and Howden, and the Vegas win chance jumped from 9% to 48%. Barbashev added more to his team's win chances than anyone in the game.

Stuart Skinner, who has taken over the Winnipeg crease since Connor Hellebuyck was traded to New Jersey in October, kept the Jets alive in overtime with a stop on Marner, the biggest save of the night. He finished 0.59 goals better than the 33 shots he faced deserved. In the shootout, William Karlsson scored the only goal; Scheifele, Connor and Gabriel Vilardi were all stopped.

The result matched the process: Vegas had 4.59 expected goals to 3.51 and wins this game 66% of the time in our replays of every shot. It also ended a four-game winless run (0-1-3) for the Golden Knights, on a night Granger described the third period as a continuing struggle for them, until it wasn't. The Jets get a point, and Scheifele gets a record nobody can take back.
headline: Scheifele makes Jets history, Vegas takes the shootout
